# MCP JavaScript API

Everything the [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) extension adds to `pb_hooks` and page code, generated from the TypeScript declarations it ships (your app's `types.d.ts` has the same, so your editor knows them). For how to use it, see its docs; for Go, the [Go API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go).

## $mcp

The app's MCP server (`/mcp`): tools map to the app's own REST endpoints.

```js
$mcp.addEndpoint({ name: "blog_publish_post", description: "Publish a draft post.", method: "POST",
  path: "/api/blog/posts/{id}/publish", inputSchema: { type: "object", required: ["id"], properties: { id: { type: "string" } } } })
```

### $mcp.addEndpoint()

```ts
$mcp.addEndpoint(def: mcp.Endpoint): void
```

Declares a tool, at the top level of a pb_hooks file. Adding the same name again replaces it.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `def` | `mcp.Endpoint` |  |

### $mcp.pathValue()

```ts
$mcp.pathValue(value: string): string
```

Escapes a value for one {name} part of a tool's path.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` |  |

Returns `string`.

### $mcp.instructions()

```ts
$mcp.instructions(text: string): void
```

Adds text to the server's instructions for the model.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` |  |

### $mcp.tools()

```ts
$mcp.tools(): string[]
```

The names of every tool.

Returns `string[]`.

## Types

### mcp.ToolRequest

The REST request a tool makes; a request transform may change it.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `string` |  |
| `path` | `string` |  |
| `query?` | `{ [key: string]: string }` |  |
| `body?` | `any` |  |
| `headers?` | `{ [key: string]: string }` |  |

### mcp.Endpoint

One MCP tool, mapped to one REST endpoint.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Tool name, e.g. "blog_publish_post". |
| `title?` | `string` |  |
| `description` | `string` |  |
| `method` | `string` | HTTP method of the endpoint. |
| `path` | `string` | Endpoint path; {name} parts come from the tool's arguments, the rest go to the JSON body. |
| `inputSchema?` | `{ [key: string]: any }` | JSON Schema of the tool's arguments. |
| `outputSchema?` | `{ [key: string]: any }` | JSON Schema of the tool's result. |
| `title?` | `string` |  |
| `readOnlyHint?` | `boolean` |  |
| `destructiveHint?` | `boolean` |  |
| `idempotentHint?` | `boolean` |  |
| `openWorldHint?` | `boolean` |  |
| `request?` | `(c: { args: { [key: string]: any }; auth: core.Record \| null; request: ToolRequest }) => ToolRequest \| void` | Shapes the request (it can't change who the call runs as). Return nothing to keep the default. |
| `response?` | `(r: { args: { [key: string]: any }; auth: core.Record \| null; status: number; headers: { [key: string]: string }; body: string; json: any; truncated: boolean; }) => any` | Shapes the result the model sees; throw for an error the model can read. |
